```{r setup}
library(mermaid2drawml)
```

## Introduction

`mermaid2drawml` converts [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) diagrams of any
type into natively editable Microsoft Word shapes (DrawingML `wps:wsp` format).
Unlike embedding a static image, the resulting shapes can be selected, moved,
resized, and reformatted directly inside Word, and each label sits inside its
shape.

Mermaid itself lays out and draws the diagram in a headless browser. The
browser reports every shape it drew, with its computed colours, line styles,
fonts and text layout, so Word output matches what you see in a browser,
including themes, `classDef`, `style` and `linkStyle`. The package integrates with
[officer](https://davidgohel.github.io/officer/), making it easy to insert
diagrams from R Markdown reports.

## Setup

Install Node.js (≥ 18) and npm, then run once after installing the R package:

```{r setup_node}
setup_mermaid2drawml()
```

The packages include the Font Awesome icon packs Mermaid needs to draw icons.
If you are upgrading from an earlier version, run `setup_mermaid2drawml()`
again: without the icon packs, Mermaid draws a placeholder instead of an icon.

You can verify the installation at any time:

```{r check_node}
check_mermaid2drawml()
```

## Basic Usage

### `mermaid_to_word()`

The primary function renders Mermaid syntax via the Node.js bridge and builds
DrawingML XML:

```{r basic}
diagram <- mermaid_to_word(
  "flowchart TB
    A[Collect Data] --> B{Quality Check}
    B -->|Pass| C[Analyse]
    B -->|Fail| D[Reject]
    C --> E[Report]"
)

print(diagram)
```

The returned `mermaid_word_diagram` object contains:

- `$xml` — the raw DrawingML XML string ready for `officer::body_add_xml()`
- `$scene` — what was drawn: `$scene$items` has one row per Word shape or group
- `$type` — the Mermaid diagram type
- `$next_id` — the next available shape ID (needed when adding multiple diagrams)
- `$links`, `$images` — the hyperlinks and pictures the XML refers to (see
  "Building documents yourself")

### `body_add_mermaid()`

For direct insertion into a Word document:

```{r body_add}
library(officer)

doc <- read_docx() |>
  body_add_par("Flowchart of the process", style = "heading 2") |>
  body_add_mermaid(
    "flowchart TB
      A[Start] --> B[Process] --> C[End]"
  )

print(doc, target = "output.docx")
```

## Using in R Markdown

In an R Markdown document, place the insertion code in an R chunk. The output
file must be a Word document (use `output: word_document`):

```
---
output: word_document
---

```{r diagram, echo=FALSE}
library(officer)
library(mermaid2drawml)

my_diagram <- "
flowchart LR
  A[Input] --> B[Transform] --> C[Output]
"

read_docx() |>
  body_add_mermaid(my_diagram) |>
  print(target = knitr::fig_path(".docx"))
```
```

> **Note**: `knitr::fig_path()` generates a unique path per chunk, avoiding
> collisions when multiple diagrams appear in the same document.

## Layout and Sizing Options

`mermaid_to_word()` and `body_add_mermaid()` take `max_scale`,
`page_width_in` and `page_height_in` as named arguments. The other arguments
below are passed on to `build_diagram_xml()`:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `page_width_in` | `NULL` | Width (inches) the diagram may fill; default: the content area of the page |
| `page_height_in` | `NULL` | Height (inches) the diagram may fill; default: the content area of the page |
| `max_scale` | 1 | Largest size relative to Mermaid's own; `Inf` fills the page |
| `font_scale` | 1 | Multiplies every text size |
| `word_font_family` | `NULL` | Font for all text (default: the font Mermaid used) |
| `min_stroke_pt` | 0.75 | Thinnest line drawn, in points |
| `align` | `"center"` | Horizontal alignment of the drawing |
| `alt_text` | `NULL` | Alternative text (default: `accDescr` or `accTitle`) |
| `links` | `"shape"` | How links are written: `"shape"`, `"field"` or `"none"` |
| `embed_images` | `TRUE` | Embed pictures; `FALSE` leaves them out |

Mermaid's own configuration goes in `mermaid_config`:

```{r layout_opts}
diagram <- mermaid_to_word(
  "flowchart LR\n  A --> B --> C",
  page_width_in = 5.0,
  mermaid_config = list(theme = "forest")
)
```

## Multi-Diagram Documents

When adding multiple diagrams to a single document, chain `start_id` / `next_id`
to avoid shape ID collisions (Word requires unique IDs):

```{r multi_diagram}
library(officer)

d1 <- mermaid_to_word(
  "flowchart TB\n  A --> B",
  start_id = 1L,
  links = "field", embed_images = FALSE   # XML that needs nothing else
)

d2 <- mermaid_to_word(
  "flowchart LR\n  C --> D --> E",
  start_id = d1$next_id,   # pick up where d1 left off
  links = "field", embed_images = FALSE
)

doc <- read_docx() |>
  officer::body_add_xml(d1$xml) |>
  body_add_par("") |>
  officer::body_add_xml(d2$xml)

print(doc, target = "multi.docx")
```

## Several diagrams in one browser launch

Starting Node and Chrome is most of the time a single render takes (a few
seconds). Give `render_mermaid()` or `mermaid_to_word()` a list of diagrams and
they are rendered in one launch, so N diagrams cost about one launch instead
of N. A character vector is still one diagram. The result is a list; a diagram
that fails holds its error condition in its slot. `mermaid_to_word()` numbers
each diagram's shapes on from the previous one's `next_id`.
`body_add_mermaid()` takes one diagram.

```{r several}
ds <- mermaid_to_word(list(
  "flowchart LR\n  A --> B",
  "pie\n  \"a\" : 1\n  \"b\" : 2"
))
failed <- vapply(ds, inherits, logical(1), what = "error")
```

## Handling problems

The package's conditions have classes and carry data:

| Condition | Field |
|-----------|-------|
| `mermaid2drawml_unsupported` (warning) | `tags`: the parts that could not be drawn |
| `mermaid2drawml_small_text` (warning) | `points`: the smallest main text size |
| `mermaid2drawml_syntax_error` | `mermaid_message`: Mermaid's own message |
| `mermaid2drawml_timeout` | `timeout`: the limit, in seconds |
| `mermaid2drawml_render_error` | any other failure of the bridge or browser |

`render_mermaid(timeout = )` limits the whole render, Node and Chrome start-up
included. `render_mermaid(svg = TRUE)` also keeps the SVG Mermaid drew, in
`svg`, to look at when a conversion seems wrong.

```{r conditions}
result <- tryCatch(
  mermaid_to_word("flowchart LR\n  A -->"),
  mermaid2drawml_syntax_error = function(e) {
    message("Mermaid says: ", e$mermaid_message)
    NULL
  },
  mermaid2drawml_timeout = function(e) {
    message("No answer in ", e$timeout, " seconds")
    NULL
  }
)

withCallingHandlers(
  mermaid_to_word("flowchart LR\n  A --> B"),
  mermaid2drawml_unsupported = function(w) {
    message("Left out: ", paste(w$tags, collapse = ", "))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
)
```

## Supported Mermaid Syntax

Every diagram type Mermaid draws is converted: flowcharts, sequence, class,
state, entity-relationship, requirement, Gantt, pie, mind map, timeline,
kanban, XY, quadrant, sankey, architecture, C4 and the others. Flowchart
node shapes that Word has a preset for (rectangles, rounded rectangles,
stadiums, diamonds, circles, hexagons, parallelograms, trapezoids,
cylinders, documents and more) become that preset; the others are drawn
from their exact outline. The README lists a verdict for each type.

Beyond shapes and text, these are carried over:

- **Text transparency** is written as Word text-fill transparency (Word 2010
  and later).
- **Gradients** on fills and lines, linear and radial, become Word gradient
  fills. Sankey bands keep their colour ramp. Word's radial gradient only
  approximates SVG's.
- **Hyperlinks** (`click X href`; only `http`, `https` and `mailto`).
  `links = "shape"` (default) makes the shape the click target and needs a
  relationship in the document, which `body_add_mermaid()` registers.
  `links = "field"` wraps the text in a `HYPERLINK` field, which is
  self-contained but links only shapes that hold text. `links = "none"` leaves
  links out.
- **Pictures**: image nodes and images in labels are embedded when the browser
  could read them. A remote image needs network access at render time;
  otherwise it is left out with a `mermaid2drawml_unsupported` warning.
  `embed_images = FALSE` leaves pictures out.
- **Icons**: `fa:`, `fas:`, `far:` and `fab:` icons and icon nodes are
  editable shapes. They need the icon packs that `setup_mermaid2drawml()`
  installs; without them Mermaid draws a placeholder.
- **Hand-drawn look**: hatching becomes a Word pattern fill in the hatch's
  direction and colour. It is an approximation: Word's pattern, not Mermaid's
  strokes.

## What comes out

Each thing Mermaid drew is one Word object you can select, move and edit.
The names show in Word's Selection Pane:

| Name | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `mermaid:node:<id>` | a node: one shape, or a group of its parts |
| `mermaid:subgraph:<id>` | a group holding the subgraph's background and members |
| `mermaid:edge:<a>-<b>` | the line of an edge from node `a` to node `b` |
| `mermaid:edge_label:<a>:<b>` | that edge's label |
| `mermaid:edge_group:<a>-<b>` | an edge grouped with its marker shapes |
| `mermaid:marker:<marker id>` | a line end Word has no end for |
| `mermaid:group:<id or class>` | parts Mermaid drew inside one element: a legend entry, an actor |
| `mermaid:icon:<node id>` | an icon, kept apart from its node's outline |
| `mermaid:image[:<id>]` | an embedded picture |
| `mermaid:shape` | a shape of a diagram without node data (block, sankey) |

Names come from Mermaid's own node and edge data. Block and sankey diagrams
have none, so their shapes are named generically (`mermaid:shape`,
`mermaid:group:…`) rather than `mermaid:node:…`.

Line ends are Word's own arrow heads where Word has the figure, sized from
Mermaid's marker and reaching the node. Ends Word cannot draw (crow's
feet, hollow triangles and diamonds, crosses, sequence numbers, a circle
or diamond larger than Word's largest end) are small shapes grouped with
their line. Boxes crossed by dividers (class, requirement and ER boxes) are
stacks of rectangles, one per compartment.

Text sits inside its shape: click a box and type. Each label keeps
Mermaid's own line breaks and is never re-wrapped; the paragraph is
aligned as Mermaid drew it (a title stays centred, member lists stay left)
and moved with the text box's insets where it was off centre. Text that
belongs to no shape, such as an axis title, is a text box of its own.

To restyle the result, pass these to `mermaid_to_word()` or
`body_add_mermaid()`:

- `word_font_family` sets one font for all text, and `font_scale`
  multiplies every text size;
- `max_scale` lets a small diagram grow to fill the page (`Inf`);
- `links` and `embed_images` say what happens to links and pictures;
- `min_stroke_pt` sets the thinnest line drawn;
- `mermaid_config` passes Mermaid's own configuration, such as
  `list(theme = "forest")`;
- `alt_text` sets the drawing's alternative text.

```{r restyle}
diagram <- mermaid_to_word(
  "classDiagram\n  class Animal {\n    +String name\n    +eat() void\n  }",
  word_font_family = "Calibri",
  font_scale = 0.9,
  min_stroke_pt = 1,
  alt_text = "The Animal class"
)
```

## Building documents yourself

`build_diagram_xml()` and `mermaid_to_word()` return `links` (`rel_id`, `url`)
and `images` (`rel_id`, `bytes`) beside `xml` and `next_id`. The XML refers to
them by placeholder ids, so when they have rows the XML alone is not
complete. Either:

- use `body_add_mermaid()`, which adds them and gives a complete document;
- pass `links = "field"` and `embed_images = FALSE` for self-contained XML,
  which `officer::body_add_xml()` can insert as it is; or
- register the relationships yourself: save each image's `bytes` as a PNG
  file and replace its `rel_id` in the XML by the file's path, and add each
  link as an external hyperlink relationship of the document body
  (`officer::docx_body_relationship(doc)$add()`), replacing its `rel_id` by
  that relationship's id. `?build_diagram_xml` gives the details.

The multi-diagram example above uses `officer::body_add_xml()` directly, so it
passes `links = "field"` and `embed_images = FALSE`. `body_add_mermaid()`
picks a free id itself.

## Not supported or deferred

- **Glued edges** (a moved node dragging its edges along) are deferred, and
  may be rejected. Word reroutes only its own preset connectors on a drawing
  canvas. Using them would mean giving up Mermaid's edge routes and the group
  that holds a diagram together. They are not planned unless a workable form
  is found. Until then, groups keep a node's parts together; move groups.
- **A browser kept alive between calls** is deferred. Rendering several
  diagrams in one call is the supported way to save launches.
- **Re-wrapping text.** Labels keep Mermaid's line breaks.
